newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends sub-$23 as support gives way.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends sub-$23 as support gives way.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures ended lower on Monday for the third day in succession, reversing most of the dollar a barrel gains posted in the middle of last week.
Jan Brent ended down 41 cents at $22.89 a barrel with a late spate of selling knocking off 15 cents after support at $23 was breached.
Brent got close to $24 last Wednesday but has since slipped back as traders took a more relaxed view of stock levels and as an early cold spell in Europe and the U.S. ended.
Dealers said uncertainty over stocks and the weather were keeping markets volatile and uncertain over direction.

"People are waiting for weather forecasts and stocks data. If you can't build stocks in the next two or three weeks you're heading for a very tight market this winter," said Bo van Wijk, vice president energy risk management at Swiss bank UBS in Zurich.
But colder weather forecast for both key heating oil markets later this week was likely to keep a floor under prices dealers said.
"No-one is really expecting the market to dump big time at this point," said an IPE broker.
Gas oil earlier had finished lower but trimmed losses near the close amid continued uncertainty over the outcome of the record delivery against expiry of the November contract.
Dec gas oil finished down $2.00 at $218.75, up from a $216.75 low.
Dec lost ground to Jan, cutting its premium by a third to $3 amid concerns the November delivery might slip into December.
Gas oil traders expect around half of the record 865,100 tonne delivery to stay in the local ARA market and for transport up the Rhine.
Some barge dealers on Monday were already complaining that barges were queueing to take delivery and that deliveries might have to extend beyond the November 30 deadline.
Others said loadings were normal by the end of the day on Monday.
